title: Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH): first response and escalation (India, ICMR)
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Labour room, PHC to district hospital, operating theatre, referral transport
summary: PPH is blood loss over 500 mL or any bleeding that deranges vital signs. Call for help, resuscitate through two wide-bore lines, start an oxytocin infusion, massage the uterus, give tranexamic acid 1 g IV within 3 hours of birth, identify the cause, and escalate through uterotonics, balloon tamponade and surgery or referral.

sections.title: Recognise PPH and red flags
items: PPH: more than 500 mL blood loss, or any amount of bleeding that causes derangement of vital parameters.
Red flags: pulse above 120/min, systolic BP below 100 mmHg, SpO2 below 95%, shock index (pulse divided by systolic BP) above 1, or deteriorating sensorium.

Find the cause: uterus flabby (atony); uterus well contracted but still bleeding (genital tract trauma, retained tissue, rupture); placenta not delivered; or bleeding with no apparent cause (coagulopathy).

sections.title: First response (all together)
items: Call for help. Rapid assessment of pulse, BP, respiratory rate and temperature; check vitals and blood loss at least every 15 minutes.
Two IV lines with wide-bore (16 to 18 G) cannulas; draw blood for grouping and cross-matching; arrange blood and blood products at the earliest.
Start Ringer lactate or normal saline, 1 litre in 15 to 20 minutes. ICMR advises 3 mL of crystalloid for every mL of blood lost in the initial acute phase; switch to blood as soon as it is available.
Oxygen 6 to 8 L/min by mask. Indwelling urinary catheter with urobag; monitor input and output.
Oxytocin 10 IU IM if not given after delivery, and start an oxytocin infusion: 20 IU in 500 mL RL or NS at 40 to 60 drops/min. Never give oxytocin as an IV bolus.
Fundal massage of the uterus. Check whether the placenta has been delivered and inspect it for completeness.

Tranexamic acid 1 g slow IV for every PPH, whatever the cause, as early as possible and definitely within 3 hours of birth; repeat once after 30 minutes if bleeding persists. Continue all other treatment meanwhile.

sections.title: Placenta and genital tract
items: Placenta not delivered: continue the oxytocin drip, palpate the uterus, and attempt controlled cord traction if the uterus is contracted. If it still does not deliver, shift to theatre for manual removal of the placenta.
Placenta delivered: continue oxytocin and uterine massage, check the placenta and membranes, and explore the uterus for retained bits, membranes or clots and evacuate them.
Uterus well contracted but bleeding continues: explore for cervical, vaginal and perineal tears and repair them.
If bleeding persists despite repair, suspect inadequate repair, uterine rupture or scar dehiscence: shift to theatre for examination under general anaesthesia and/or laparotomy.

sections.title: Atonic PPH: uterotonics and tamponade
items: Bimanual uterine compression plus pharmacotherapy, and increase the oxytocin infusion to 10 to 20 units/h.

Add any of these alone or in combination, as available: methylergometrine 0.2 mg IM or slow IV, repeat after 15 minutes up to 5 doses (1 mg); carboprost (PGF2 alpha) 250 micrograms IM, repeat every 20 minutes up to 8 doses (2 mg); misoprostol 800 micrograms rectally or sublingually.
Methylergometrine is contraindicated in hypertension, severe anaemia and heart disease. Carboprost is contraindicated in asthma.
Bleeding not controlled: intrauterine balloon tamponade (condom catheter), with continued bimanual compression and oxytocin.
Aortic compression can reduce blood loss as a short-term measure while definitive steps are arranged.

sections.title: Refractory bleeding, coagulopathy and referral
items: Surgical options in escalating order: uterine compression sutures; systematic devascularisation (uterine, then ovarian, then internal iliac artery ligation); hysterectomy. Uterine artery embolisation in selected women where available.
If bleeding continues without an apparent cause, check coagulation and give blood and blood components.

Refer early to a higher centre if blood transfusion, exploration or surgery are not available. Transport with IV fluid containing oxytocin running, preferably with the uterine or vaginal tamponade in situ, and a non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG) if available.
Timely action and referral save lives: do not wait for a falling Hb or hypotension before escalating.

sections.title: After bleeding is controlled
items: Uterine massage every 15 minutes for the first 2 hours.
Vital signs every 10 minutes for 30 minutes, every 15 minutes for the next 30 minutes, then every 30 minutes for 3 to 6 hours or until stable.
Continue oxytocin infusion at 5 to 10 units/h; total oxytocin must not exceed 100 IU in 24 hours.
Monitor input and output, transfuse as indicated, and counsel the woman and family about what happened and the plan.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Giving oxytocin as an IV bolus (can cause hypotension).
Delaying tranexamic acid beyond 3 hours, when it no longer helps.
Using methylergometrine in pre-eclampsia or hypertension, or carboprost in asthma.
Continuing to give uterotonics for bleeding from a tear or rupture with a well-contracted uterus.
Referring without IV access, oxytocin running, tamponade in situ or an escort.

drugs.name: Oxytocin
drugs.dose: 10 IU IM if not given at birth. Infusion 20 IU in 500 mL RL or NS at 40 to 60 drops/min; 10 to 20 units/h during bimanual compression; 5 to 10 units/h once controlled
drugs.notes: No IV bolus. Maximum 100 IU in 24 hours.

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.dose: 1 g slow IV; repeat once after 30 minutes if bleeding persists
drugs.notes: For all PPH, as early as possible and within 3 hours of birth.

drugs.name: Methylergometrine
drugs.dose: 0.2 mg IM or slow IV, repeat after 15 minutes, maximum 5 doses (1 mg)
drugs.notes: Contraindicated in hypertension, severe anaemia, heart disease.

drugs.name: Carboprost (15-methyl PGF2 alpha)
drugs.dose: 250 micrograms IM, repeat every 20 minutes, maximum 8 doses (2 mg)

drugs.name: Misoprostol
drugs.notes: Useful where injectables or cold chain are limited.

drugs.name: Ringer lactate or normal saline
drugs.notes: Replace with blood and components as soon as available.
